_README: CROSS-LANGUAGE GOLDEN VECTORS for #3304 S1's rule tier (#3304 S2).
Two readers assert against this one file, in one CI run:
crates/loomux-engine/tests/triage_vectors.rs  -> loomux_engine::triage (the SOURCE OF TRUTH)
test/orchtriageeval.test.ts                   -> scripts/orch-triage-eval.cjs (the MIRROR)
That is the whole of the reuse seam. The rules are hand-written prefix tests
over &str, so there is no data an engine export could hand the script; what
CAN be shared is the ANSWERS, and a divergence in either direction reddens
the side that moved. The mirror's vocabulary is pinned separately by a scan
of triage.rs in the JS test, because a vector cannot see a Rust rule that has
no vector; that test also asserts every rule and never-reason below is
exercised by at least one case.
A case is:
text                  the delivery text, verbatim
human_actor           the audit row's actor is the human
merge_queue_enabled   the repo's merge_queue: block is on
policy                {enabled, kinds}; kinds [] means every kind
expect.kind           classify()
expect.never          never_triaged(), or null
expect.decision       decide(), as {action, reason} | {action, rule} | {action, pr}
Texts are SYNTHETIC, written to the shapes orrerix emits. No line of a real
group's agent-authored prose is checked in here.
THE THREE NUMBER TESTS ARE NOT THE SAME TEST, and the four `+`/`-` cases at
the end of this file are what pins that. `drive_notice` and `plan_chunk`
parse with `u64`/`u32::parse`, which accepts a leading `+` and refuses a
`-`; `run_completed` tests `chars().all(is_ascii_digit)`, which refuses
both. Nothing orrerix emits carries a sign, so these are unreachable in
production — they are here because the mirror had assumed one rule for all
three and the divergence was invisible to both pins until a case existed
(review round 1, finding 2).
